envelope.text: ADOPT-BOUNDED: a backend that cannot answer

why:
LANDED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 C8): `rcl_service_server_is_available(node, client, &is_available)`, rcl's name and three arguments, reached from `<rcl/graph.h>`. ENVELOPE (stated on the declaration): a backend that cannot answer (XRCE without participant enumeration) returns `RCL_RET_UNSUPPORTED` and leaves `*is_available` untouched, where rcl always answers; `node` is checked and otherwise unused, the deviation `rmw_vtable.h` already declares for this slot. This supersedes the 2026-09-03 target (reshaping `rclc_client_service_is_ready`): since phase-492 C carries rcl's names, so rcl's own spelling is the one to ship, and both `rclc_` spellings keep their shapes for one release instead of one being broken in place. Test: `tests/run/service_server_is_available.c`. PRIOR ROW: the theirs half of a name we already ship twice. rcl spells it `rcl_service_server_is_available(node, client, bool*)`; ours are `rclc_client_server_available` and `rclc_client_service_is_ready`, and service/'s `cpp:Client::service_is_ready` records the decision that `service_is_ready` is the name to keep (rclcpp and rclrs both use it) and `c:client_server_available` the one to drop. Recorded here as the rcl-side half so the pair is complete. CORRECTED 2026-08-27 (phase-379 W5): the previous text claimed "two real signature deviations ... no `node` parameter and no allocator". There is ONE. `rcl_service_server_is_available` takes no allocator either -- its three parameters are `(const rcl_node_t *node, const rcl_client_t *client, bool *is_available)`, verified in `docs/reference/api-surface/rclc.json` under `rcl/graph.h` -- so there was nothing to drop, and citing it as a deviation invented an alignment we already have. The real deviation is the missing `node`, and our ABI declares it in those words: `packages/core/nros-rmw-abi/include/nros/rmw_vtable.h:571`, "an image has no node object to pass -- the client reaches its session directly". Note the vtable SLOT already carries rcl's exact spelling -- `service_server_is_available(const rmw_client_t *, bool *out_available)` at :575 -- so the disagreement this row records is entirely in the public C/C++/Rust entry points ABOVE the vtable, not in the ABI. This is the ONE member of rcl's `rcl/graph.h` we implement (every other member reports `theirs-only`, verdicted `gap` or `divergence`), and TWO of the three backends implement it. CORRECTED 2026-09-11 (phase-428 W13.c): this row read "implemented by exactly one backend" for four days after `fa61bde7a` made that false, and its three file:line citations had all moved. As measured on `main`:

  * ZENOH answers from the session's liveliness subscription -- `ZenohServiceClient::service_is_ready`, `packages/rmw/zenoh/nros-rmw-zenoh/src/shim/service.rs:1016`, walking the domain-wide graph cache for an `SS` token (phase-428 W13.a/b).
  * CYCLONE answers from the DDS discovery cache -- `nros_rmw_cyclonedds::client_server_is_available`, `packages/rmw/cyclonedds/nros-rmw-cyclonedds/src/service.cpp:1452`, wired at `packages/rmw/cyclonedds/nros-rmw-cyclonedds/src/vtable.cpp:365`. It mirrors upstream `rmw_cyclonedds_cpp`'s `check_for_service_reader_writer`: matched readers on the request writer AND matched writers on the reply reader, paired by `serviceid` user data where a server advertises it. Test `packages/rmw/cyclonedds/nros-rmw-cyclonedds/tests/service_server_available.cpp` asserts false -> true -> false across a server's life, so the answer is CURRENT and not latched, which is what issue 1087 was about.
  * XRCE keeps the slot NULL, DELIBERATELY and permanently (`packages/rmw/xrce/nros-rmw-xrce/src/vtable.c:96`, reasoning at the slot). The Agent owns the DDS participant, so matched-endpoint state lives Agent-side and micro-XRCE-DDS-Client has no read for it: no `dds_get_matched_*`, no built-in topic readers, no participant enumeration. The one fact the session has -- the Agent acknowledged `create_requester` -- says the CLIENT's endpoints exist and nothing about a server, so answering from it would be issue 1087's optimistic default one layer down. NULL is the ABI's spelling of "cannot answer" (`packages/core/nros-rmw-abi/include/nros/rmw_vtable.h:649`, which named XRCE as its case at `:646`), and `CffiClient::service_is_ready` surfaces it as `Err(Unsupported)`.

DISPOSITION `adopt-bounded`, and XRCE is the bound. Not `refuse-loud`: that is a COMPILE-time construct and the backend is chosen at RUNTIME through the named registry, so no spelling of the verb can refuse on one backend and compile on another. Not `absent`: the name is present and callable everywhere. What is weakened is the ANSWER, inside the stated three-answer envelope -- `Ok(true)` / `Ok(false)` / `Err(Unsupported)` -- of which XRCE permanently occupies the third, stated at the slot and in the ABI header where a reader meets it.
